paper_sections.title: Brain activation patterns associated with cue reactivity and craving in abstinent problem gamblers, heavy smokers and healthy controls: an fMRI study
Results for performance data and craving ratings
Correlations between BOLD activation, subjective craving, BDI-II and CAARS

description.value: The study investigated cue reactivity and craving-related brain activation during gambling and smoking picture viewing in treatment-seeking problem gamblers, heavy smokers and healthy controls.

spans.text: In this neuroimaging study, cue reactivity in problem gamblers (PRG) was compared with cue reactivity in heavy smokers (HSM) and healthy controls (HC).

design.value: An fMRI event-related picture cue-reactivity paradigm compared gambling, smoking-related and neutral pictures across problem gamblers, heavy smokers and healthy controls, with additional craving correlation and FTND subgroup analyses.

spans.text: A functional magnetic resonance imaging event-related cue reactivity paradigm, consisting of gambling, smoking-related and neutral pictures, was employed in 17 treatment-seeking non-smoking PRG, 18 non-gambling HSM, and 17 non-gambling and non-smoking HC.
In addition, the South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS; ) was administered as a measure of problem gambling severity.

The main inclusion criterion for PRG was current treatment for gambling problems.

Exclusion criteria for all groups were: age under 18 years; difficulty reading Dutch; use of psychotropic medication; a lifetime diagnosis of schizophrenia or psychotic episodes; a 12-month diagnosis of manic disorder, assessed with the respective sections of the Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI; ); current treatment for mental disorders other than those under study; physical conditions known to influence cognition or motor performance (e.g. multiple sclerosis, rheumatic disease); positive urine screen for alcohol, amphetamines, benzodiazepines, opioids or cocaine; consumption of more than 21 units of alcohol per week.
The PRG were recruited from two Dutch addiction treatment centers.

task_description.value: A picture two-choice response task presenting gambling, smoking-related, neutral and low-level baseline pictures in random order.

spans.text: A picture two-choice response task was used (for examples of pictures, see ).

A functional magnetic resonance imaging event-related cue reactivity paradigm, consisting of gambling, smoking-related and neutral pictures, was employed in 17 treatment-seeking non-smoking PRG, 18 non-gambling HSM, and 17 non-gambling and non-smoking HC.

instructions.value: Participants had to press a response button with their left index finger when a face was present in the picture and their right index finger when no face was present; they were requested to respond within 5 seconds.

spans.text: In the gambling, smoking-related and neutral pictures, participants had to press a response button with their left index finger when a face was present in the picture and had to press a response button with their right index finger when no face was present.

stimuli.value: Thirty gambling pictures, 30 smoking-related pictures, 30 neutral pictures and 30 low-level baseline pictures were presented randomly.

spans.text: Thirty gambling pictures, 30 smoking-related pictures, 30 neutral pictures and 30 low-level baseline pictures were presented randomly, with the restriction that a stimulus of the same stimulus category was not presented more than three times in a row.

task_performance_measures.value: mean reaction time to the pictures in each stimulus category

spans.text: The performance parameter for the task was mean reaction time to the pictures in each stimulus category.

modality.value: T2*-weighted echo planar images, sensitive to blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) contrast

spans.text: While participants performed the task, T2*-weighted echo planar images, sensitive to blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) contrast were acquired (35 axial slices, voxel size 3 × 3 × 3 mm, interslice gap 0.3 mm, matrix size 64 × 64 mm, bandwidth 90 kHz, TE 35 ms, repetition time 2.28 seconds), covering the entire brain except for the inferior regions of the cerebellum.
The scanning session lasted 15 minutes; each of the gambling, smoking-related and neutral pictures was presented once.
